lifecycle: FastAPI lifespan starts a daemon thread; startup scan then interruptible Event wait; stop/join on shutdown
source_query: issues.status=ISSUED AND due_date < UTC midnight(today+3days); Mongo cursor batch500

rules.DUE_SOON: due UTC calendar date minus today =2
rules.OVERDUE: due UTC calendar date before today; one initial per due version

catchup: Only the present meaningful state; does not replay missed DUE_SOON/TODAY or every overdue day
dedupe: TYPE:issue_id:normalized_UTC_due_timestamp; unique DB index and setOnInsert; four concurrent scanners verified
source_recheck: Exact issue/user/status/due version re-read immediately before write
reservations: Optional V1 alerts skipped; no invented expiry
renewal: No current renewal API; changed due version verified in isolated Mongo test
limitations: An already stored reminder stays in history after return/due change.
Source recheck and notice insert are not a multi-document transaction; a concurrent return in the tiny interval can still race.
Hourly catch-up needs Core running; no durable separate scheduler.
